title: K-flat normalized descent of localized extension tensor comparisons to strict coefficient towers
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small Grothendieck site, $R$ a sheaf of commutative rings, and $V\in\mathcal C$. Use $R_V=R|_V$ on the localized site $\mathcal C/V$ [def-pur-localized-ringed-site], module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], their ordinary unbounded derived categories with localization functors $Q$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and exact localized-site extension $j_{R!}$ [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact]. Let $S_\bullet=(S_n,s_n:S_{n+1}\to S_n)_{n\geq1}$ be a strict inverse sequence of sheaves of commutative $R$-algebras; all structural maps preserve $R$ and the unit [def-weil-inverse-system]. On the diagram site of [lem-weil-pbc-diagram-site-realization], write $\Delta$ for the constant diagram and set
$$\mathcal R_S(M)=\Delta M\otimes^L_{\Delta R}S_\bullet,\qquad
\mathcal R_{S|_V}(K)=\Delta K\otimes^L_{\Delta R_V}(S_\bullet|_V).$$
Derived tensor uses sheaf tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] and flat-term K-flat representatives [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. Let $J_R$ be termwise $j_{R!}$ on strict $R_V$-module towers and its exact derived functor. For every $K\in D(R_V)$ there is a unique natural isomorphism
$$\rho_K:\mathcal R_S(j_{R!}K)\xrightarrow{\sim}J_R\mathcal R_{S|_V}(K)$$
with the following representative normalization. On every flat-term K-flat complex $P$ representing $K$, after the canonical localization comparisons for exact extension and derived tensor, $\rho_{QP}$ is $Q$ of the chain isomorphism of strict towers whose level $n$, degree $i$ map is the inverse sheaf projection comparison
$$j_{R!}P^i\otimes_R S_n\xrightarrow{\sim}j_{R!}(P^i\otimes_{R_V}S_n|_V).$$
These are the tensor comparisons of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-slice-extension-tensor]. The isomorphism is natural also in morphisms of the $R$-algebra tower, commutes with all $s_n$ before localization, and is independent of the chosen representative under its canonical derived comparisons. Its evaluation at $n$ is the restriction of scalars of the $S_n$-linear isomorphism
$$(j_{R!}K)\otimes_R^L S_n\xrightarrow{\sim}j_{S_n!}(K\otimes_{R_V}^L S_n|_V),$$
where $j_{S_n!}$ is localized-site extension with coefficient ring $S_n$. On an ordinary module, the comparison carries the extension of the map $p\mapsto p\otimes1$ to that same map after extension. No flatness of $R\to S_n$, no surjectivity of $s_n$, and no boundedness or completion hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: Choose a flat-term K-flat resolution $P\to H$ of a complex representing $K$. Exact extension represents $j_{R!}K$ termwise and carries this resolution to a quasi-isomorphism. The total-tensor extension lemma gives K-flatness of $j_{R!}P$. Its terms are flat as well: for an exact sequence $A\to B\to C$ of $R$-modules, restrict it by exact $j^*$, tensor with flat $P^i$, and apply exact $j_{R!}$. The sheaf projection isomorphisms identify the resulting exact sequence with its tensor by $j_{R!}P^i$. Thus every flat-term K-flat representative, not just the chosen resolution, is sent to one.

source.place: Tag 06YS, lemma-K-flat-resolution; sites-modules.tex Tags 03DJ and 0E8I, lemma-extension-by-zero-exact and lemma-j-shriek-and-tensor; acyclic-tensor extension argument

proof.text: Use the small inverse-sequence index category in the diagram-site realization. Each evaluation $e_n$ is an exact module inverse image, and jointly the evaluations detect zero objects and exact sequences: the equivalence sends objects and morphisms to their literal components. Apply the ordinary cochain pullback tensor comparison to $e_n$; its coefficient ring identification is $e_n\Delta R=R$. It identifies evaluation of a total tensor with the total tensor of the evaluations, with its actual differentials. Evaluation also commutes with direct sums, as a left adjoint. Consequently $\Delta P$ has flat terms and is K-flat: for an acyclic diagram complex $A$, each evaluation of $\operatorname{Tot}(A\otimes\Delta P)$ is $\operatorname{Tot}(A_n\otimes P)$, hence acyclic; joint detection gives acyclicity of the diagram tensor. The identical argument applies on $\mathcal C/V$ and to $\Delta(j_{R!}P)$. For flatness of each diagonal term, use the same evaluation argument with an exact sequence in place of $A$.

source.place: Tags 06YN and 06YU, K-flat test and total tensor; diagram-site evaluation and its ordinary ringed-pullback tensor comparison

proof.text: The normalized one-sided tensor computation on the two diagram sites now identifies $\mathcal R_S(j_{R!}QP)$ with $Q((j_{R!}P\otimes_R S_n)_n)$, and $\mathcal R_{S|_V}(QP)$ with $Q((P\otimes_{R_V}S_n|_V)_n)$. No K-flatness of $S_\bullet$ is used: the first factor is the flat-term K-flat complex certified in Step 2. Termwise extension on towers is exact, since exactness is levelwise and $j_{R!}$ is exact. Its exact localization comparison therefore identifies $J_R\mathcal R_{S|_V}(QP)$ with $Q((j_{R!}(P\otimes_{R_V}S_n|_V))_n)$. These computation comparisons are natural in maps of K-flat representatives and in all coefficient-tower maps. The identification is one of strict towers: under the module equivalence of the diagram-site realization, the presheaf tensor at $(n,W)$ is $j_{R!}P^i(W)\otimes_{R(W)}S_n(W)$ and its structure map from level $n+1$ to level $n$ is $x\otimes y\mapsto x\otimes s_n(y)$, since $\Delta(j_{R!}P)$ has identity transitions. The evaluation comparisons of Step 2 send a local pure tensor $x\otimes y$ to $x\otimes y$. Hence the two composites $j_{R!}P^i\otimes_RS_{n+1}\to e_n\operatorname{Tot}(\Delta(j_{R!}P)\otimes_{\Delta R}S_\bullet)$ agree on presheaf generators, and the uniqueness clause of module sheafification makes them equal; so the transitions are $1\otimes s_n$. The same holds on $\mathcal C/V$ with $P\otimes_{R_V}S_n|_V$.

proof.text: For any local $R_V$-module $M$ and $R$-algebra sheaf $S$, use the extension presheaf with summands indexed by $u:W\to V$. The inverse projection comparison is the map $[m]_u\otimes s\mapsto[m\otimes s|_{(W,u)}]_u$. It is additive and $R(W)$-balanced, respects restrictions (both indices become $u\circ a$ along $a:W'\to W$), and hence extends through tensor and module sheafification by the cited bilinear extension theorems. Its inverse is induced on each summand by $[m\otimes s]_u\mapsto[m]_u\otimes s$, since $(S|_V)(W,u)=S(W)$. The two composites fix every pure tensor in every summand, so sheafification uniqueness makes them identities. This gives precisely the sheaf projection isomorphism, with its direction as in the statement. It is $S$-linear for the action on the second tensor factor; $j_{R!}(M\otimes S|_V)$ with this action is the underlying $R$-module of $j_{S!}(M\otimes S|_V)$: both are sheafifications of the same direct sums with that sectionwise action. The module sheafification interface identifies their underlying abelian sheaves and actions.

source.place: Tags 03DI, 03CY and 0E8I, lemma-extension-by-zero, lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules and lemma-j-shriek-and-tensor; explicit generator calculation

proof.text:
Apply Step 4 to $M=P^i$ and $S=S_n$ in every degree and level, obtaining $r_P$. Naturality of the projection comparison in the first variable gives $r_P(d_P\otimes1)=j_{R!}(d_P\otimes1)r_P$, so this is a chain isomorphism. Naturality in the second variable gives the strict transition equation
$$j_{R!}(1_P\otimes s_n|_V)\,r_{P,n+1}=r_{P,n}(1_{j_{R!}P}\otimes s_n).$$
Thus $r_P$ is an isomorphism of strict towers before localization. For a map of algebra towers $a:S_\bullet\to T_\bullet$, both composites in its naturality square take $[p]_u\otimes s$ to $[p\otimes a_n(s)|_V]_u$. For $s=1$, the formula takes $[p]_u\otimes1$ to $[p\otimes1]_u$; hence it intertwines the two extensions of the scalar-unit map. Every assertion here is an equality of maps of sheaves or complexes, established on the presheaf generators by Step 4.

source.place: Tag 0E8I, lemma-j-shriek-and-tensor, naturality in both variables, with the explicit unit and transition formulas

proof.text: Conjugate $Q(r_P)$ by the computation comparisons of Step 3. This supplies an isomorphism between the restrictions of the two stated derived functors to the homotopy category of flat-term K-flat complexes. It is natural there: it is natural in chain maps by Step 5; a homotopy $h$ is sent to $h\otimes1_{S_n}$, which is a homotopy since $S_n$ is in degree zero, and exact extension is additive. The resolving-class equivalence $W^{-1}\mathcal P_{R_V}\simeq D(R_V)$ and the localization universal property descend this transformation uniquely to $\rho$. Descend the inverse $Q(r_P^{-1})$ as well. Faithfulness of restriction makes both composites identities, so $\rho$ is a natural isomorphism. Its component on every $QP$ is, by construction, the normalized $Q(r_P)$ required in the statement.

proof.text:
For a derived object represented through $q:QP\xrightarrow{\sim}K$, naturality fixes the component explicitly as
$$\rho_K=(J_R\mathcal R_{S|_V})(q)\,\rho_{QP}\,(\mathcal R_Sj_{R!})(q)^{-1}.$$
The uniqueness of descent in Step 6 makes this formula independent of $P$ and $q$, with precisely the canonical computation comparisons, and shows that any natural isomorphism with the representative normalization equals $\rho$. For a coefficient-tower morphism, the two composites in its desired derived naturality square agree after restriction to every flat-term K-flat $P$ by Step 5; faithfulness of restriction gives their equality on $D(R_V)$. In particular these are comparisons of the strict-diagram derived objects, obtained from $r_P$, rather than chosen lifts of levelwise derived maps.

source.place: Tag 06YU and categories.tex Tags 04VG/04VK, uniqueness and full faithfulness of localization

proof.text: Fix $n$ and evaluate the representative equation for $\rho$ at $n$. Exact evaluation has its termwise localization comparison; Step 2 identifies the evaluated total tensor with the ordinary total tensor. Its one-sided normalization identifies the resulting map with the derived comparison computed by $j_{R!}P\otimes_R S_n\to j_{R!}(P\otimes_{R_V}S_n|_V)$. To retain the coefficient action, view scalar extension as module pullback for the identity underlying topos with ring map $R\to S_n$, and likewise on the slice. The K-flat pullback computation identifies $(j_{R!}K)\otimes_R^L S_n$ with the $S_n$-complex $j_{R!}P\otimes_R S_n$, and $K\otimes_{R_V}^L S_n|_V$ with the $S_n|_V$-complex $P\otimes_{R_V}S_n|_V$. Exact $j_{S_n!}$ computes its derived functor on this latter complex. Step 4 gives an $S_n$-linear chain isomorphism between these representatives and identifies its scalar restriction with the evaluated $r_P$. Exact restriction of scalars and uniqueness of resolving-class descent therefore give the claimed $S_n$-linear derived isomorphism and identify its restriction with $e_n\rho$. No step used flatness of $S_n$ over $R$, surjectivity of a transition, boundedness, or completeness.
